```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = FALSE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE, fig.width = 10)
library(amorem)
fmt <- function(x, d = 0) formatC(x, format = "f", digits = d, big.mark = ",")
```

# Bundled datasets

amorem ships the event logs and covariates below, each loadable with
`data(...)`. The tables and figures on this page are computed from them when
the page is built. The [data catalogue](data-catalogue.html) documents a wider
collection, including datasets whose licences do not allow amorem to
redistribute them.

## Event logs

```{r inventory}
ev <- list(
  classroom_events = list("Classroom (McFarland 2001)", "face-to-face, minutes", "minutes"),
  social_evolution_calls = list("Social Evolution calls (Madan et al. 2011)", "phone calls", "days"),
  social_evolution_friendship = list("Social Evolution friendship survey", "tie changes", "days"),
  radoslaw_email = list("Manufacturing company email (Nurek & Michalski 2020)", "email", "days"),
  college_msg = list("CollegeMsg (Panzarasa et al. 2009)", "instant messages", "days"),
  email_eu_core = list("Email-EU-core, one department (Paranjape et al. 2017)", "email", "days"),
  copenhagen_calls = list("Copenhagen Networks Study calls", "phone calls", "days"),
  copenhagen_sms = list("Copenhagen Networks Study text messages", "text messages", "days"),
  us_leader_visits = list("US leader-to-leader visits 1945-2019", "state visits", "days"),
  football_results = list("Men's international football since 1872", "matches", "days"),
  ucdp_dyads = list("UCDP armed conflict dyads 1946-2025", "conflict dyad-years", "year"),
  alien_invasions = list("Alien species first records 1880-2005", "species -> region", "year"))
inv <- do.call(rbind, lapply(names(ev), function(nm) {
  e <- new.env(); data(list = nm, envir = e); x <- get(nm, e)
  s <- if (nm == "alien_invasions") x$species else x$sender
  r <- if (nm == "alien_invasions") x$region else x$receiver
  t <- if (nm == "ucdp_dyads") x$year else if (nm == "alien_invasions") x$stop else x$time
  span <- diff(range(t))
  data.frame(object = sprintf("`%s`", nm), data = ev[[nm]][[1]], kind = ev[[nm]][[2]],
             events = fmt(nrow(x)), actors = fmt(length(unique(c(s, r)))),
             span = sprintf("%s %s", fmt(span, if (span < 100) 1 else 0), sub("^year$", "years", ev[[nm]][[3]])))
}))
knitr::kable(inv, row.names = FALSE)
```

`congress_bills_118` holds hyperevents: each of its
`r fmt(nrow(congress_bills_118))` bills has one sponsor and a set of
cosponsors (mean `r fmt(mean(lengths(congress_bills_118$J)), 1)`, largest
`r fmt(max(lengths(congress_bills_118$J)))`), from
`r format(min(congress_bills_118$date))` to `r format(max(congress_bills_118$date))`.
Actor attributes come in `classroom_actors`, `social_evolution_actors`,
`copenhagen_actors`, `congress_members_118` and `radoslaw_hierarchy`.

## What each log looks like

For each event log: the network of the actors in its busiest pairs, then when
the 30 most active of them are active. The [data catalogue](data-catalogue.html) adds a
close-up of single events and the counting processes of the busiest pairs.

```{r views, results = "asis"}
source("data/catalogue/helpers.R")
bundled <- c("classroom_events", "social_evolution_calls", "radoslaw_email", "college_msg", "email_eu_core",
             "copenhagen_calls", "copenhagen_sms", "us_leader_visits", "football_results", "ucdp_dyads",
             "alien_invasions", "congress_bills_118")
for (nm in bundled) {
  p <- readRDS(file.path("data/bundled", paste0(nm, ".rds")))
  cat(sprintf("\n### `%s`\n\n", nm))
  if (p$kind == "hyper") {
    cat(knitr::knit_child(text = c(sprintf("```{r v-%s, fig.width = 10, fig.height = 6, fig.alt = 'Hyperevents of %s over time'}", nm, nm),
                                   "plot_hyper_timeline(p$view, p)", "```"), quiet = TRUE, envir = environment()))
    cat("\n", cap_hyper_timeline(p), "\n")
  } else {
    cat(knitr::knit_child(text = c(sprintf("```{r n-%s, fig.width = 7, fig.height = 5.4, out.width = '60%%', fig.align = 'center', fig.alt = 'Network of the most active actors of %s'}", nm, nm),
                                   "plot_network(p$view)", "```"), quiet = TRUE, envir = environment()))
    cat("\n", cap_network(p), "\n")
    cat(knitr::knit_child(text = c(sprintf("```{r t-%s, fig.width = 10, fig.height = 6, fig.alt = 'Activity of the most active actors of %s over time'}", nm, nm),
                                   "plot_timeline(p$view, p)", "```"), quiet = TRUE, envir = environment()))
    cat("\n", cap_timeline(p), "\n")
  }
}
```

## Who is active

Share of all events in which the most active 10% of actors take part, and the
Gini coefficient of actor activity (0 when all actors are equally active):

```{r concentration}
conc <- do.call(rbind, lapply(names(ev), function(nm) {
  e <- new.env(); data(list = nm, envir = e); x <- get(nm, e)
  a <- if (nm == "alien_invasions") c(x$species, x$region) else c(x$sender, x$receiver)
  n <- sort(as.numeric(table(a)), decreasing = TRUE)
  g <- { y <- sort(n); k <- length(y); sum((2 * seq_len(k) - k - 1) * y) / (k * sum(y)) }
  data.frame(object = sprintf("`%s`", nm),
             top10 = sprintf("%.1f%%", 100 * sum(n[seq_len(ceiling(length(n) / 10))]) / sum(n)),
             gini = sprintf("%.2f", g))
}))
knitr::kable(conc, row.names = FALSE, col.names = c("object", "events with the top 10% of actors", "Gini"))
```

Logs with highly concentrated activity are where count statistics carry sender
and receiver activity rather than dyadic history; see
[Real-data analysis](real-data-analysis.html) for a comparison with and without a
sender frailty.

## Global covariates

- `enso_nino34`: tree-ring reconstruction of the winter Niño3.4 anomaly,
  1301-2005 (see `vignette("species-invasion")`); `oni`: the instrumental
  Oceanic Niño Index since 1950.
- `daily_weather`: daily temperature and precipitation at Boston (Social
  Evolution, 2008), Santa Ana (CollegeMsg, 2004), and Warsaw and Wroclaw
  (manufacturing email, 2010).
- `public_holidays`: public holidays for the same countries and years.

They take one value at a time for every pair, so their effects are estimated
with time-shifted sampling (`sample_non_events(shift = "exponential")`); the
[email case study](case-email-global.html) does this with the clock.

`dist_matrix` holds distances between 56 US states and territories, used by the
validation experiments.

## Time conventions

Event times are days since the first event, except `classroom_events`
(minutes since the start of the class), `ucdp_dyads` (year) and
`alien_invasions` (years `start` and `stop`). Where the source gives clock
time, `attr(x, "unix_origin")` holds the Unix time of `time = 0`:

```{r origins, echo = TRUE}
format(as.POSIXct(attr(radoslaw_email, "unix_origin"), origin = "1970-01-01",
                  tz = "Europe/Warsaw"), usetz = TRUE)
format(as.POSIXct(attr(college_msg, "unix_origin"), origin = "1970-01-01",
                  tz = "America/Los_Angeles"), usetz = TRUE)
```

## Sources and licences

```{r licences}
lic <- data.frame(
  object = c("`radoslaw_email`, `radoslaw_hierarchy`", "`copenhagen_*`", "`congress_bills_118`, `congress_members_118`",
             "`us_leader_visits`", "`ucdp_dyads`", "`football_results`", "`alien_invasions`",
             "`daily_weather`, `oni`, `enso_nino34`", "`public_holidays`", "`dist_matrix`",
             "`college_msg`, `email_eu_core`", "`classroom_events`, `classroom_actors`",
             "`social_evolution_*`"),
  source = c("Harvard Dataverse doi:10.7910/DVN/6Z3CGX", "Figshare doi:10.6084/m9.figshare.7267433",
             "US GPO govinfo BILLSTATUS bulk data", "Harvard Dataverse doi:10.7910/DVN/2ZNR5R",
             "Uppsala Conflict Data Program", "github.com/martj42/international_results",
             "Dryad doi:10.5061/dryad.x69p8czpv", "NOAA NCEI and CPC", "Nager.Date API",
             "US Census TIGER/Line", "SNAP (Stanford)", "networkDynamic R package", "goldfish R package"),

```

Each object's help page (`?radoslaw_email`, `?ucdp_dyads`, ...) gives the
reference to cite. Please cite the original source of any dataset you use, in
addition to amorem.
